title: Why Women Thrill to True Crime
author: Malin Hasselblad
content:
![Why Women Thrill to True
Crime](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/08/Screenshot-2026-08-21-at-7.26.35
---AM.png)

I've seen theory after theory about how he did it, or that he drove her to do
it. Is it just the slant of my algorithm, or do you feel similarly?" This
Reddit post summarizes the forensic fan fiction frenzy of the ongoing trial of
Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother charged with the horrifying crime of
strangling her three young children. At first glance, there is little mystery
there. Lindsay's defense attorney doesn't dispute that she did it, but argues
that she is not legally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum
psychosis.

Online, however, many think that the case needs a better plot. TikTok
[_users_](https://www.tiktok.com/@emily_ruth__/video/7671789768165838093?q=patrick%20Clancy%20did%20it&t=1787126304793&ref=compactmag.com)
[_accuse_](https://www.tiktok.com/@truecrime.elowen/video/7666467539618106654?q=lindsay%20clansey%20poll&t=1787124930120&ref=compactmag.com)
Clancy's former husband, Patrick, of framing his wife. There is talk that he
drugged her, that he hired a body double to keep his alibi airtight. The
videos appeal to a feeling of female camaraderie; we're all just sticking up
for a sister in need, they tell us--while poring over every gruesome detail
and hoping for a dramatic ending. "I can't wait for the Netflix documentary
about this so we're able to find out the husband did it," as one commenter
puts it. Despite the abundance of evidence suggesting otherwise, a sinister
husband concealing a crime makes the story all too perfect of an entry in the
true crime genre.

In America, a third of podcast listeners regularly choose true crime shows.
Women are [_almost twice as likely_](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-
reads/2023/06/20/true-crime-podcasts-are-popular-in-the-us-particularly-among-
women-and-those-with-less-formal-education/?ref=compactmag.com) as men to do
so: 44 percent of female podcast listeners consume the genre regularly,
compared with 23 percent of men, according to a 2022 Pew survey. The same
gender pattern holds in Britain and Europe. The female appetite for violence
extends beyond stories presented as fact. The author Wendy Jones recently
[_examined_](https://www.ft.com/content/3b00d881-078d-4eca-9492-3c82f9c57728?ref=compactmag.com)
the _Sunday Times_ list of Britain's ten bestselling paperback novels, which
are written primarily for a female audience, and discovered that nine of them
featured the murder of a woman.
